scope: website frontend, data pipeline, deduplication, monitored-community catalog and source validation

findings.finding: data/listings.json was previously reduced to a small manually reconstructed set; historical/base records need to be rebuilt from the earlier commit and reconciled with the latest scan before claiming full coverage.
findings.action: keep the latest scan and verified overrides authoritative for current cases; restore missing historical/base records through a controlled reconciliation rather than deleting them.

findings.finding: the old UI cleanup merged cards solely by visible fingerprint, which could merge two different units with identical floor/area/layout/price.
findings.action: UI cleanup now requires at least one shared active source platform in addition to the same visible fingerprint.

findings.finding: the catalog injection script listed outdated communities and had a filter event mismatch.
findings.action: catalog updated to the 13 monitored communities and now dispatches the input event used by the main filter.

findings.finding: source-status.json and batch-scan-report.json still contain earlier verification timestamps until the next scheduled scan completes.
findings.action: next GitHub Actions scan should refresh source validation timestamps and reports.

findings.finding: some stored links are community/search pages rather than true individual listing pages.
findings.action: keep them out of the direct-link UI when URL validation rejects them; replace them only after an actual listing URL is obtained.

findings.finding: the current scan ledger correctly reports partial coverage and must not claim 100% completeness when platform aggregate counts exceed verified records.
findings.action: retain the yellow partial-completion state until every source can be checked listing-by-listing.

hardRules: Never guess floor, block, area, parking or direct URL.
Never merge distinct units merely because floor/area/layout are similar.
Never treat historical actual-registration data as an active listing.
Never claim complete scanning when only aggregate platform counts are known.
Never treat 403/429/timeout as proof that a listing is sold or removed.
